doc.title: Giacomo Gates interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 29, 2015 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Digital sales, Pandora and YouTube
summary: DMP Records, music made less important by easy access, and bad YouTube recordings.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: You entered the business, I would say, in the digital age, right?
Do you have an opinion about the way music is sold these days?

Yeah. Well the very first company that I got hooked up with, DMP Records, the first CD company to do quadrasound — that was interesting, because they were an audiophile company, not really a jazz company. So they were into the recording of it. But I know what you mean, you mean the sale of the music? Is that what you were referring to?
Yes. It occurs to me because you’re on Pandora and everybody’s on —
And do you feel that you ever get any compensation for the fact that anybody can access your music at any time.

You know it’s nice that people can hear you that formerly couldn’t. On the other hand, it makes — I don’t know — it makes the music less important. If it’s that easy to get it then what’s the big deal. I know record companies are in a spin. They don’t know how to make it happen. You know, Facebook, YouTube, I mean I have no idea how much stuff is on YouTube of things that I’ve done. And you know what? I’m not that crazy about it. Because if — I think I’m a pretty in-tune singer. But I’ve heard stuff on YouTube it’s like my God, what key am I singing in? Sometimes, you know that little 42 dollar thing that they’re recording you on is junk. So by the time they post it, it sounds bad, it looks worse, so somebody who doesn’t know what you do or somebody who doesn’t have a real recording looks at it and goes, “I’ll never go see that.”
And you have no control over who puts up what.

No. I mean you could say, “please, no live recordings.” Yeah right. I mean if people have something in their pocket and they have it on. So not only do they get a bad recording but they have the rustle of their clothing to go with it.
